texts.facts: The plaintiff is proprietorship firm duly engaged in the business of manufacturing and marketing of scrubber/scrubbing Brushes pads, under the trademarks "PARASNATH" and another trademark "PARAS". The plaintiff firm carries on its business in Delhi by itself Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. and the plaintiff has firm has its principal place of business as well as warehouse and distributors in Delhi. 3. That the plaintiff firm is duly registered its trademark "PARAS" and also got registered its artistic work as 'PARASNATH" and the registration of the same stands renewed from time to time by the Trademark Registry and the said Trademarks, on account of renewal, are valid and subsisting in favour of the plaintiff till date. 4. That the brand "PARAS" and "PARASNATH" are well known brand in the business of home appliances in India and the plaintiff firm on its hard work and labour created trust in the mind of public and present the registered brand of plaintiff firm is known as most pre- mium brand targeted and adopted by the users throughout India. 5. That the trademarks of the plaintiff firm are registered under the provisions of the Trademarks Act, 1999. That the said trademarks and the other trademarks are registered in Trademark registry of India, details of which are as below: MARK LOGO Registration Registration Valid Till Class No. date PARASNATH 1966346 17.05.2010 17.05.2020 21 PARAS 1703379 25.06.2008 25.06.2008 21 Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. 6. It has been further stated that plaintiff has spent huge amount of money in advertising and promotion of its products under the trade- mark 'PARAS' and 'PARASNATH' in India. The said advertisement and the promotion are done by the plaintiff firm through various print as well as electronic media such as newspapers, magazines, radio commercials, TV commercials, pamphlets, etc and also through hoard- ing etc. and that on account of good quality and standards of manufac- turing and even introducing new technologies and by putting its skill- ful and untiring efforts in advertising and marketing, goods of the plaintiff has acquired an enviable reputation in India. 7. It has been further stated that the net/sale and revenue of the plaintiff firm per year as follows: Sale Net profit. 2018 Rs.3,55,37,399/- Rs.12,75,573/- Parasnath Enterprises vs Sunil Aggarwal And Ors on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21738100/ 2 2017 Rs.1,59,54,074/- Rs.7,72,781/- 2016 Rs.92,47,348/- Rs.7,39,792/- 8. That the defendants are a business entity engaged in the busi- ness of manufacturing, storing and selling infringing goods bearing the falsified trademarks 'PARAS', 'PARASNATH' 'PARASBRIGHT' and 'ASR PARAS' from its premises. Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. 9. That the defendants are arrayed based on the John Doe principle as applicable in India, as the same being unknown identity. 10. It has been further stated that during a market survey in the first week of May, 2016 it came to the knowledge of the Plaintiff firm that the defendants are clandestinely manufacturing, finishing, storing and selling scrubber/scrubbing Brushes under the trademark "PARAS", 'PARASNATH", PARAS BRIGHT" and "ASR PARAS" or decep- tively and confusingly similar trademarks which are much inferior quality than the products of the plaintiff and the labels attached and the trademarks embossed on the impugned product of the defendant is same/similar in design and appearance, as those used by the plaintiff firm and thus defendant is blatantly infringing the registered trade- marks of the Plaintiff Company in complete contravention of the law of the land and these infringing goods are readily available in the mar- kets of Delhi and other parts of Delhi/NCR. That the photocopy of the infringing product of the defendant displaying the falsified marks and the photographs of the original product displaying the original trade- marks and logos are annexed to the plaint . Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. 11. It has been further stated that the investigator of Plaintiff Com- pany visited premises of defendants and purchased / procured inform- ing goods bearing the impugned trademarks of the Plaintiff firm and Defendants do not issue any receipt for its products. 12. It is further stated that studying the essential features of the products of the plaintiff and those of the defendants and also the trade- marks and logos affixed by the plaintiff on its original products with those of the marks and logos affixed by the defendants it becomes ob- vious that the defendants is selling its products in the guise of the products of the plaintiff firm and the finished scrubber of the defen- dants ae of much inferior quality than those marketed by the plaintiff firm. On examination of the infringing goods of the defendants and original goods of the plaintiff of the plaintiff firm have differences and similarities as shown in para 18 of the amended plaint. Parasnath Enterprises vs Sunil Aggarwal And Ors on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21738100/ 3 13. It is further in stated that defendant with malafide intentions have infringed the registered trademarks and logos of the plaintiff by affixing same/similar trademarks 'PARAS' 'PARASNATH', 'PARAS BRIGHT' and 'ASR PARAS' logos of the plaintiff and that the malafide and dishonest intention of the defendants is evident from the fact that they have adopted all the unique and distinctive features of the plaintiff's trademarks 'PARAS' and 'PARASNATH' and defen- dants have used the trademark 'PARAS' 'PARASNATH', 'PARAS Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. BRIGHT' and 'ASR PARAS' logo of the plaintiff without knowledge and prior permission of the plaintiff firm and thus liable for a legal ac- tion. 14. It is further stated that the defendants have acted to cause dam- age to the purchasing public by selling them the spurious products in the name of the plaintiff firm and earning illegal profits on account of the unlawful use of deceptively and confusingly similar trademarks 'PARAS' 'PARASNATH', 'PARAS BRIGHT' and 'ASR PARAS' logo of the plaintiff firm and goodwill of the plaintiff and if the defen- dants is not restrained from continuing the same the plaintiff shall con- tinue to have irreparable losses of business as well as injure to the goodwill of its products. 15. On the application of plaintiff filed under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 CPC, the interim stay was granted restraining the defendants from us- ing the trademark and logos 'PARAS' and 'PARASNATH', on any scrubber/scrubbing brush and other product till NDOH and Ld. Local Commissioner was appointed to inspect the premises of defendant who accordingly inspected the given premises and filed his report. 16. Summons of the suit were issued to the defendant. Service was effected upon the defendants and they appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement.
texts.arguments: Both the defendants in their respective written statements have commonly taken the plea that plaintiff has suppressed the material facts and has not approached the court with clean hands and that plain- tiff is itself a pirator of the said trademark and is not the honest and concurrent user as the trademark 'PARAS' is the registered trademark of a firm namely M/S Paras Miracle Poly Products Pvt. Ltd situated at 351, 10th Mile Stone, Nagar Kalyan Road, Ahmad Nagar - 414103 since 22.09.2004. It is further stated that plaintiff has itself surrepti- tiously adopted the mark 'PARAS' and 'PARASNATH' and a pira- tor of the trademark himself cannot seek injunction relief against third party. Thus, plaintiff is not the exclusive user of the mark 'PARAS' and 'PARASNATH', which has been used by the abovementioned company prior to the plaintiff. It is the case of the defendant no. 1 that he is using the word 'ASR PARAS' and 'PARAS BRIGHT' and further it is the case of de- fendant no. 2 that he is using the word 'PARAS' for its products. It is stated that the mark of the plaintiff i.e. PARAS and PARASNATH are in no way concerned with the marks 'ASR PARAS' and 'PARAS BRIGHT' of defendant no.1 and that of 'PARAS' of defendant no. 2. The word 'PARAS' is the common dictionary word in which no one can claim a copyright and the manner in which the said word is written Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. which gives it the distinctive meaning and in which a person may have a copyright but the marks of the defendants are entirely different from plaintiff's marks. 19. It is further the case of both the defendants that their font, de- sign and colour are distinctive and there is no colourable imitation of the mark of the plaintiff. It is further stated that the marks of the plaintiff are having different colour, font and design with horizontal narrow lines in blue colour whereas the defendants marks are plainly shown as 'ASR PARAS' and 'PARAS BRIGHT' and 'PARAS' in dif- ferent font and design and judging by the eye alone, they appear to be totally different and there is least resemblance among the said marks of the plaintiff and the defendants. 20. The varieties of "confusion" have been thus identified, by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Shree Nath Heritage Liquor Pvt. Ltd. v. Allied Blender & Distilleries Pvt. Ltd. It is settled law that overall similarity has to be seen in considering the similarity and side by side comparison should not be made in order to determine the similarity. Pawan Kumar has been examined as PW1 and in view of the same, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the plaintiff. Reliance is placed on Iqbal Bashit vs. N. It is settled law that in civil suits plaintiff can examine his attor- ney holder as a witness such attorney holder cannot testify about the Parasnath Enterprises vs. Sunil Aggarwal and ors. facts that are exclusively within the knowledge of the plaintiff. For ex- ample, if the facts are not in the personal knowledge of attorney holder but the same are in the knowledge of the plaintiff, the attorney holder cannot testify it, but if the attorney holder was involved in transaction and has personal knowledge of the facts he can testify as a witness. Reliance is placed on a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court titled as Janki Vashdeo Bhojwani and anr. vs. Indusind Bank Ltd. 2005 (2) SCC 217. 66. The court has gone through the evidence filed by the attorney holder as a witness and his cross examination and there is nothing from which it can be said that there is any material for which he could not testify being solely within the personal knowledge of the principal i.e. plaintiff. Further there was no question in the cross examination of this witness which required personal knowledge of the plaintiff hence this argument has no merit. 67. It is further argued by Ld.
